newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL RUBBER ENDS MIXED ON BRITISH, ITALIAN BUY TALKS.
newsitem.headline: KL RUBBER ENDS MIXED ON BRITISH, ITALIAN BUY TALKS.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended mixed on Thursday, with buyers ignoring the market save for two rumoured purchases by Britain and Italy, trade sources said.
"We're trying hard to hold back prices but business is very slow in East Asia," said a rubber trader in Kuala Lumpur.
Bargain hunting, coupled with fears of a volatile ringgit and excessive rubber stocks in Thailand, pummeled sentiment, said dealers.
Government trade sources reported hearing that 60 tonnes of RSS1 was sold to Britain while another 80 tonnes of the material was contracted to Italy at an unknown price, both for August.
Traders could not confirm the deals.
"I haven't heard anything for today," said a trader. "Where did this come from?"
Another said: "There's no one coming up to buy and there's no paying up for what they have bought."
At the close, the RSS1 for September buyer was officially quoted at 247.50 cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg, unchanged from Wednesday's close.
The SMR20 for September buyer closed at 246.50, down once cent from Wednesday.
Dealers offered the SMR 20 at 244 cents a kg, the SMR CV at 290 cents, SMR L at 272, SMR 5 at 253, SMR 10 at 246 and drum latex at 189.
The INRO five-day average price was at 192.50 Malaysia/Singapore cents a kg on August 6, down the 192.59 on August 5. The daily indicator was at 191.83 compared to 191.78.
Malaysia-based shipping brokers quoted freight rates for rubber from Malaysia to Rotterdam at $700 per 20-ft container, and $1,400 per 40-ft container.
